resources.string: This version (%1$s) is not a published one: no update is offered to it. Install a published version to receive updates.
Ciné Doury is up to date
You have the latest published version, %1$s.
You ignored this version: it is no longer offered at startup.
The file is checked: it is the one published. Android will ask you to confirm the installation, then Ciné Doury will restart.
Android installs an app from elsewhere only once you allow it, once and for all. Open the settings, turn Ciné Doury on, then come back here.
Google TV: Settings → Apps → Security & restrictions → Unknown sources → Ciné Doury.
NVIDIA Shield: Settings → Device Preferences → Security & restrictions → Unknown sources → Ciné Doury.

The installed version is not signed with the same key as the published ones (a development version is not): Android would refuse to replace it. Uninstall Ciné Doury once from the settings of the TV, then install %1$s; your profiles will have to sign in again.
The update did not go through
GitHub does not answer. Check that the TV can reach the Internet, then try again.
GitHub limits the checks for now. Try again after %1$s.
GitHub limits the checks for now. Try again in an hour.
The answer of GitHub cannot be read. Try again later.
The downloaded file is not the one that was published. Nothing was installed; try again.
Android refused the installation. Try again; if it happens again, send the diagnostic report.
